The Unified Payments Interface, UPI, is India's system for instant payments between bank accounts by mobile phone. It was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India, a body set up by banks under the Reserve Bank of India.

A user links a bank account to an app and gets a simple ID, then pays by typing it or scanning a QR code. Payments clear in seconds, at any hour, and are free for most users. Because UPI is a shared public network, any bank or app can join, from Google Pay to small fintech start ups.

It took off after the banknote demonetisation of November 2016 left India short of cash, and again during the Covid lockdowns. Street vendors and tea stalls now take payment by QR code. UPI now carries billions of payments a month, more than any other real time payment system. It is part of the digital public infrastructure India built on Aadhaar identity numbers, and other countries have studied it, much as they once studied Kenya's M-Pesa.
